newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, in Kremlin, vows to protect pensions.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, in Kremlin, vows to protect pensions.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, looking tired but determined during brief televised remarks while in his Kremlin office on Thursday, assured elderly Russians they would continue to receive their pensions.
He was shown briefly speaking to TV cameras and the head of the upper house of parliament during his fifth visit to the Kremlin since he came down with pneumonia in both lungs exactly a month ago.

During his remarks, the president sharply criticised a proposal made by the head of the country's pension fund to reduce pensions for those who continue working. The proposal has been widely criticised in the press and by opponents.
"I can firmly say as president that this will never happen," Yeltsin said. "Pensions for the ordinary pensioner will be preserved today, tomorrow, the day after and as long as we live."
Russian women above the age of 55 and men above 60 are eligible for pensions, but many continue to work to make ends meet.
"Not the president, nor the government, nor the Federation Council, nor the Duma have even given thought to this," Yeltsin said, referring to both houses of parliament.
He called the suggestion by the head of the pension fund a "terrible blunder".
